you will not be able to function. This is not because they lack love, or because you lack love for them. Moreover, there is no provision to accept two Gurus. The Guru will impart advice or guidance to only a select few. Nothing else will be obtained. Whatever you receive comes solely from the *Brahmavit* and *Brahmavaryan* Gurus. Beyond these four categories, there are other Gurus. They are born in accordance with the times. God Himself ordains their birth through a special decree. Certain Gurus born without inherent supernatural powers (*Siddhi*) are examples of this.

Ramananda Swami is the Guru of Kabir Das. Based on the *Bhaktavijayam* and the Puranas, the soul of Kabir Das is understood to be that of a *Brahmarshi*. Kabir Das was not born of a womb (*Yoniputra*). His birth occurred under extraordinary circumstances. It is not something that can be easily explained and comprehended here. It is said that the *Trimurtis* requested Kabir Das to be born in a specific manner. Only then could they have him act according to their intentions. At that point, Kabir Das informed the *Trimurtis* that he could not be born of a womb. He agreed to incarnate only after they promised to facilitate his birth through an alternative means. We are listening to the history of such a great soul. However, what that great soul speaks about the world, the Guru, and the lineage encompasses vast and profound domains. It is then that we truly comprehend the greatness of the Gurus.

In South India, obtaining Gurus of such magnificence has been exceedingly rare. Even if such an occurrence were to happen, our inclination is merely to subordinate them to a deity rather than preserving their legacy in accordance with their greatness. The reason for this is the advent of Shudra governance here. By 'Shudra' here, it refers to the class-Shudra (*Varga-shudra*), not the caste-Shudra. This Shudra was compelled to do everything. Among us, excluding the Brahmin, Kshatriya, and Vaishya, all others are considered Shudras. By establishing governance through the class-Shudra, diverse types of subjects came under the rule of a single monarch. This implies that the king lacked discernment. The one called a king attained power through brute force, not by legitimately occupying the position of a Kshatriya. There is historical evidence for this. The history of Travancore itself serves as an example. The *Ettuveettil Pillamar*, Marthanda Varma, and the *Ettara Yogam* were all members belonging to the Shudra category. Following this, women were adopted from a Kshatriya household. This Kshatriya family was the Mavelikkara family. These are all historical facts. We have not had the opportunity to reflect upon this.

Extremely arduous labor was extracted from the Shudra. History from a thousand years ago does not indicate the existence of caste here. The caste system seen today has emerged merely within the last millennium. Prior to that, the only castes were the aforementioned four foundational classes (*Varnas*).

You will understand the greatness of the Guru only when you comprehend the blunder we have committed. Upon coming to South India, the very concept of the Guru faded away. Apart from offering verbal praises, you have never had the administrative experience of respecting and obeying a Guru. You are also ignorant of your own domestic traditions. This lack of knowledge caused the position of the Guru to degrade so drastically. Due to the absence of a Guru tradition (*Guru Sampradaya*), we have encountered numerous afflictions.

What is the reason the people in South India lacked a complete Guru tradition? The era during which we treated each other as untouchable castes upon sight was not insignificant. That is where you committed your first error. That is what brought a king here. Subjects raised in such a country were prohibited from acquiring education. They were not allowed to handle wealth. The state administration was never intended for those devoid of education and wealth. Thus, they were trampled and suppressed. Those who ruled with tyranny, eating and drinking whatever they could extract, along with a few corrupt officials who thrived on bribes, created a new class. This class was forced to perform all kinds of labor. Due to harsh and menial labor, a community grew in utter ignorance, much like wild grass. Meanwhile, a few within this system sat back and enjoyed luxuries.

Under the cover of such comforts, the local rulers acquired the power to do anything and destroy anything. The king also needed their power. They were given positions of honor. You do not need to know any of the Vedas, Shastras, or Upanishads behind this. If you go out at dawn and work until dusk, you will get a measure (idangazhi) of paddy. The work is for an idangazhi of paddy. Not even for an idangazhi of rice. Out of this idangazhi of paddy, a little is given to the shop to buy salt or chili. The rest is parboiled, pounded, cooked, and consumed to pass the time. Today you might say it is starvation. No. How long ago did the habit of wearing good clothes come about? In those days, none of the workers could afford a dhoti costing more than ten chakras. Even on a taluk basis, you might find about ten such houses. There would certainly be no more than that.

How can we acquire any kind of knowledge while leading such a life? Instead of leading a life endowed with such knowledge, our inability to attain it is due to the grand schemes of the kings. It is impossible even to count the rich people who showed a kind of perversity, stretching their legs to immerse themselves in all the worldly pleasures, making the poor work to help them and destroying them through labor, and those who tolerated these debaucheries to lead an opportunistic life by exploiting them.

When transitioning from the rule of the Ettuveetil Pillamars to the reign of Marthanda Varma, Marthanda Varma's own history states that he beheaded those who applied intellect, logic, and knowledge. Because if they lived, his own head would not remain. The administrative histories before us show that the women of these Ettuveetil Pillamars were captured and married off to fishermen, while the men were beheaded. The government was the 'Ponnu Thampuran' (the golden king). It is said that the Ponnu Thampuran ruled and washed away everything here. Who was washed away? The poor - they were washed away as he pleased. Anyone of some standing was beaten to death. The others were ruled using brute force, much like the British administration did, and through this rule, they became the masters.

The British struck with the butt of their guns. Then it was set right. When this happened, the followers of Vedic rituals and the godfathers here stepped down and started offering enchanted flowers. They chanted mantras after praying for many days. When those who had said they could just pluck and throw them away realized that the butt of the gun would hit their own backs, they cleverly became their slaves. Not only did they become slaves, but they also betrayed the country to them. Gradually, it became about paying tribute. There are records that the king here paid eight lakhs as tribute in those days. Yet, the royal rule continued like an empty shell. We can understand without asking anyone that the people who lived under this rule had no awareness or discretion about good and evil. In this context, demanding "we want freedom, we want freedom," a struggle was waged as a challenge against the British for about a couple of hundred years, and freedom was attained.
Guruvani
March 1982

When freedom was achieved, some of the culture of the British, Muslims, and Christians had spread here. The people handling the administration here—the Hindu administration—out of allegiance to the West, distorted the very history of India, like cutting and shining a torch. Swinging a fire torch in a circular motion from a distance makes it look like a massive fireball, doesn't it? But it doesn't have that much size. Similarly, they do not know the story. They could not understand anything about the history of the Hindus—or what glory their ancient history held. What happened because of this? The nation and politics vanished from here. Everything became like a mashed heap of coir pith. In this state, like handing over governance to an ignorant donkey, power is being handed over to anyone, saying, "You rule." Everyone is ruling.

But even though you have done all this, God has brought about one thing. The time of the author of the Gita says - 'Sambhavaami Yuge Yuge' - what needs to happen in every age will happen in the world from time to time. It means that if you do not accept it, it will kill you. Accepting it is a duty that people must do wisely. It is an undoubted fact that this will come. Now, Christianity, which is only about two thousand years old, and Islam, which is about fifteen hundred years old, are saying things in a renewed form of this. If you look at their history, you can see that before that, things proceeded without any order or discipline.

Due to the government here as mentioned earlier, the flaw of not being able to know gurus and great souls, and the ignorance of people who lived without education, wealth, and enlightenment, we do not know the guru tradition. Or even a puranic tradition is unknown to us. What happened to us from this is complete slavery. However, an era called the hybrid age by the author of the Gita has happened here. Everything is a hybrid today. Starting from humans, birds, and animals to plants, there are hybrid species today. There is adulteration and hybridization in fertilizers, milk, and all food items. Unadulterated honey to be added to medicines is not available. In this state, the age of hybridization has arrived.

Now religious syncretism will come. It is about to come soon. When religions realize they cannot win by fighting each other, a syncretism will emerge. Even though caste is spoken of now, there is a certain shame in explicitly expressing caste loyalty. Still, they will ask secretly - is this the only name? Is there any extension to the name? In the past, when people from places like Thalassery, Kannur, and Kozhikode came to Thiruvananthapuram, one would only see their names. Without adding a tail (caste surname), with just this name here*, when they couldn't get their things done, they too started adding tails. Now everyone has added names like Nair, Pillai, Menon, and Kurup. But in the north, in their native place, this is not there. Thalassery, Kannur, and Kozhikode, if you go to these places, this can be clearly known. From this, we must understand that it is this caste that has destroyed us. This caste, how can we remove it from here? If you want to know the Gurus, if you want to develop love for them, this caste feeling must leave your hands. Otherwise, when you develop love for your caste, you will be unable to absorb the greatness of the Guru. Haven't you heard some people saying - 'Everything is fine, but if only he had been born in the womb of a Nair woman ...'. Then it would have been great', they would casually say. Just imagine how deeply this matter is seated within. This should not happen to us.

In one part of the Manusmriti, it is stated that the varnas of great souls should not be asked. Varnas do not refer to castes. It refers to the four varnas mentioned earlier. He might be a Shudra. Even so, it should not be asked. As an example for this, it is said that the source of a river and the birthplace of great souls should not be investigated. But what are we doing? It is only after inquiring where he was born, who he is, and whose son he is, that we begin to accept a Guru.

If you are to understand the part referred to as the 'lie of the Gurus', there are some other things as well. We can never know these Gurus completely. Moreover, we do not know how to respect and understand the position of the Gurus. Because we suffered the misfortune of not knowing, and because we did not get the opportunity to respect and understand this, we have developed a lot of ignorance inside Kerala or even in South India itself. We can change this only if you become more aware. Only then will you understand if you are told what is called the 'lie of the Guru'. Let me tell you a small method of the Guru's lie. If you look at the history of the Prophet, or if you look at the history of Jesus, Kabir Das, or Ramananda, certain qualities in them
*(In Thiruvananthapuram)

can be seen standing out. What is this knowledge that stands out so much? The Prophet was a person who lived like an ordinary man until the age of forty. He was the son of an ordinary carpenter who carved and sold idols. The history of Jesus is also like that. But how high they stand in history. Mere words - to say in our language, 'ethereal voices' (Ashariri) - were truthfully being received only by that great man. Those received words, written down from time to time, became scriptures. Similarly, several great souls belonging to that, and several disciples following that, emerged. Or the 'Moulvis' who came after that. They took whatever someone wrote down, added to it, and made it into many things. But, even in that, many fabricated stories have crept in. A book has been published recently, making it seem like Muslims are the cause of all the transformations in this world. It has only been two years. But surpassing all this comes the history of the 'Bahaullah' people. When these two histories do not agree with each other, they will fight. Even now, all these Muslim countries are fighting. It is only going to worsen soon. This religious tangle is the reason for this.

Pakistan was separated from the people in India today. When they got the government in their hands, how many great souls did they kill. They tore apart and killed those who worked for the people and the country. The reason for that is a curse. We must believe that they were not able to see the Prophet in a perfect manner. Because they killed the children of the Prophet and others. It is seen that the heads of seventy-three people were chopped off. That curse is what remains in them today. Whenever their government comes, it will chop down a few. Look at the history of Iran and Iraq. Aren't these all countries in Asia? How many leaders were killed in Pakistan and Bangladesh. They are killing countlessly everywhere there. But it is not known outside.

In India, under the rule of Hindus, killing in this manner is rare. Not that it doesn't exist, it does. We have the history of shooting down Mahatmaji and the history of ruling by imprisoning great men. Why has all this been said? It is for you to know the destruction caused by what you did to Gurus and great souls.
Guruvani
April 1982

The British ruled with greater diplomacy and through deceptive methods. They introduced their education and wealth in a distinct manner and ruled for a period. By doing so, they established an administrative system among the people. However, they carried away all other resources from here to transform their snow-clad country into a paradise. Considering all these factors, those of us who lived under such regimes lacked the fortune to properly comprehend the true greatness of the Guru.

An example of this is Kabirdas, the incarnation of the previously mentioned Sage Suka. He was an individual without any formal literacy. He accepted Ramananda, who attained enlightenment through the path of devotion rather than mystical powers, as his Guru. However, despite being bestowed with the merit and eminence to serve as a Guru even to Kabirdas, Ramananda remained unaware of his own identity and the purpose of his arrival. Why did God bring Ramananda into this world without revealing this to him? This was a divine decree. Only Kabirdas, who possessed no significant formal education or scriptural knowledge, could accomplish all this and reveal the true nature of the Guru. Kabirdas was innately enlightened from birth due to the wisdom acquired in his previous incarnations. We perceive Kabirdas as a sage who foreknew future events and recognized the true nature of individuals. It was through Kabirdas that the greatness of Ramananda was brought to light. Dismissing him as a Muslim boy by caste, all the Brahmins who had hitherto continuously chanted the Vedas came forward in opposition. However, with the arrival of the Siddha known as Gorakshan, all these Brahmins fled in fear. Even when Kabirdas was merely a young child, he was severely beaten and expelled three or four times. It was only after enduring all these trials that he finally departed from the Gurukula.

After serving the Guru and traversing all other stages, Kabirdas returned. It was Kabirdas who revealed to the Guru his own true identity and the magnitude of his greatness. This Guru (Ramananda) himself was unaware that he was the one destined to perform and orchestrate all these deeds. What is the reason behind this? It is a divine mechanism established by God to prevent arrogance. Kabirdas, the incarnation of Sage Suka, has profoundly stated that even if all the water in the world's oceans were transformed into ink and all the trees were uprooted to serve as pens, it would still be impossible to exhaustively write about the greatness of the Guru.

Then what constitutes the deception of this Guru? How do we truly comprehend this Guru? Simultaneously, although they share the sacred bond of Guru and disciple, this Ramananda repeatedly beat and expelled this disciple. He was banished from the ashram as if he were slain. Yet, Kabirdas could neither disrespect that Guru nor utter a single word of disparagement. This profound restraint stems from a vibrant, living devotion towards the Guru. It is exceedingly rare to find such unblemished disciples. Equally, it is difficult to find Gurus completely devoid of deception. Both these realities coexist.

Suppose we encounter such Gurus; how would we recognize them? How should we embrace these Gurus? Among them, there are 'Kalantara Gurus' (Gurus of an era) and those who manifest every two thousand or five thousand years. It is said that there are only five such 'Kalantara Gurus' in a Yuga. How, then, do we comprehend entities who appear like Sri Krishna, the Prophet, or Sankaracharya? The philosophical essence of what they have all articulated in various languages remains fundamentally identical. We end up elevating such Gurus to the status of deities, merely seeking refuge beneath their divine guise. This is precisely why Sankaracharya was depicted in the divine embrace of 'Tripurasundari'. This represents a distinct logic employed by scholars. Even in their ignorance, they find a certain comfort in documenting such narratives. When scholars recorded this, the common people inherently believed it to be the truth. Only a Guru who directly imparts knowledge to a child can articulate its specific characteristics. How can disciples truly recognize a Guru of such a profound lineage who lived two or three millennia ago? Or how would the Gurus themselves know? It is stated that Agastya lived as the ultimate, exemplary model for all Gurus. What definitive attributes can be ascribed to this Agastya? Or how can one accurately characterize Sankaracharya? What is to be inferred from the assertion that Mahavishnu was kicked—it signifies the decisive act of a sage. Hasn't this been encapsulated in a narrative? Therefore, as I previously mentioned, once a mortal truly ascends to the state of a sage, he transcends deities, capable of even kicking or spitting upon them. Even if regarded as a mere fabricated tale, the underlying principle is vividly evident. A sage exists beyond the Trinity. Beyond that realm is the Sanyasi (ascetic). He is the one who retreats and eventually returns as a Guru.

How can this Guru be comprehended? This is precisely where we fail to grasp the divine deception of the Guru. No intellect born and nurtured within this world can fathom this, because it is a deliberate deception orchestrated by the Divine. Therefore, it remains beyond our inherent knowledge. Hence, individuals in close proximity to the Gurus must possess elevated consciousness; otherwise, peril is inevitable. There is no merit in merely proclaiming that your Guru is supreme and that you are obedient followers. The true benefit is bestowed only upon those who stand close and diligently strive to align themselves in harmony. Thus, if those accompanying these Gurus lack a magnitude, intellect, and capability equal to the Guru, they will inevitably fail to understand the Guru. Only such a profound disciple can respectfully comprehend this Guru. The history of Kabirdas serves as an irrefutable proof. Numerous disciples accompanied Ramananda; countless individuals accepted discipleship and subsequently departed. None of them proved to be genuinely capable. That is precisely why it is stated that there must be a disciple who profoundly knows the Guru. Only he can authentically reveal the Guru to this world.

Do not harbor the assumption that you can independently comprehend and inherently believe in the Guru. Through familiarity, you might marginally incorporate it into your thoughts and foster belief. Consequently, you can also acknowledge the Gurus chronicled on paper. However, if the term 'Guru' embodies a supernatural force appointed by nature, transcending nature itself, you cannot comprehend it through such conventional means. It remains unknowable through written Vedas or poetry. Nothing substantial has been documented about the true Guru in any of those texts to date. This profound reality can only be realized through direct experience. Thus, if a 'Kalantara Guru'—a monumental Guru and great soul who manifests once in two or three thousand years—instructs you to conduct yourself in a specific manner and engage exclusively in prescribed practices, and if you comprehend and act accordingly, you will inevitably experience it as the absolute truth.
Guruvani
May 1982

Regardless of one's level of education, a person cannot truly know the Guru. He can merely articulate perspectives by referencing the Puranas and Upanishads. These texts were authored by poets, erudite scholars, and a few individuals with practical experience. However, none of them can accurately write about the true Gurus. An illustrative example is that when studying this Guru, one realizes he has traversed through countless eras across numerous incarnations—as a wanderer, a devotee, a yogi, an enlightened soul, and a man of action. Following all these arduous phases, he incarnates as various forms of Gurus across seven distinct births. These seven births are profoundly destined for attaining the divine presence of God.

This is a matter you must be exceedingly careful about. Through these seven births, they emerge as Gurus in various forms and depart. If not within a single epoch, they take these seven births over the course of seven epochs. Who is capable of writing the history of such a Guru? Can it be accomplished by anyone other than a disciple who has arrived alongside the Guru? It is impossible for anyone else. That is why it is said that when studying the Guru, or while living alongside the Guru, one must carefully preserve the exact words spoken by the Guru. He needs to study nothing else. That itself is a glory. Through seven births as a Guru, he undertook seven kinds of responsibilities, and by the seventh state, he had departed. Subsequently, he is born again only in accordance with the mandate of the Divine Will (*Brahmanishchayam*). We cannot ascertain how the Divine Will is going to be proclaimed. How can one write the history of this person? No one but a disciple who reveals this person can write it. However, suppose that Guru has a thousand experienced disciples. The thousand individuals will perceive it in a thousand different ways. If what is perceived in a thousand ways is documented in a thousand different manners, how will people understand this Guru? It would be akin to an auspicious moment being ruined into a complete mess. Consequently, one cannot truly know this Guru. In reality, very few would even venture to write about such a Guru.

One can write the biography of the Guru. However, it should not be written merely to demonstrate who the Guru is today. That is a perilous undertaking. This Guru might occasionally speak many things without premeditation. There are both positive and negative elements in what is spoken thus impulsively. The reason is that this Guru is not someone who has lived a highly systematic and disciplined life. In the perspective of a scholar, this will be perceived as a deficiency. A ritualist, regardless of who he is, will address him merely as the son of Chanku the butcher. He can only perceive him in that manner. He fails to comprehend why this individual was born as the son of this Chanku. Only by being born in such a manner can he impart certain truths to the world. Had he been born as the son of a wealthy man or a king, a different complication would arise there. The births of the Prophet and Jesus serve as examples of this. But the birth of Moses is not analogous.

The Prophet was born as a remarkably handsome individual and the son of a sculptor. He was also a wealthy person in his life. Furthermore, he was a member belonging to the royal lineage of that land. By the standards of that era, sculptors were not ordinary individuals. Because they meticulously studied this art and elevated it to a prestigious status, it was managed by the kings of that time. However, stating this does not imply that the Prophet did not experience poverty. Poverty was imposed upon him during a particular phase. He was born into this impoverished state, sustaining himself through sculpture, precisely to convey the reality of such hardship. Yet, to impart teachings, there must be one possessing exemplary knowledge. That is why, despite lacking formal education in literacy, he possessed profound knowledge in all these matters. The words of the Prophet are monumental words. The reason for this stems from his distinguished lineage.

Moses was a knowledgeable individual born into a relatively affluent family. He was raised in grandeur, yet learned through the experience of poverty. There is a distinction regarding the birth of Moses. He was fortunate by birth. Having been raised in prosperity, he demonstrated the stark contrast between prosperity and poverty to the people, presenting himself as entirely impoverished so as to be acceptable to the destitute.

Jesus did not arrive in that manner. A highly qualified individual came and spoke, yet you failed to accept it. Therefore, he was ordained to be born in a place devoid of any notable heritage to speak of. When Jesus was brought forth in this way, since the local populace lacked the capacity to accept it, they engaged in conflicts, waged wars, and created sheer turmoil. How he came to be a Guru for us remains a profound question even today. Time elapsed as they continued to ponder this. The kingdom was ultimately destroyed. Studying such figures presents somewhat of a complex conundrum. It is perhaps better to simply believe without deeply analyzing it. Consequently, if we are to explain and comprehend this, it is merely necessary to study their history to some extent.

When we begin to comprehend such great figures, if this is their nature, who would be the previously mentioned 'Guru across epochs' (*Kalanthara Guru*)? How can we possibly encapsulate them in words? This is precisely why Kabir Das, who incarnated as Suka Brahmarshi, articulated it in this manner. That Suka has been undergoing birth and death ever since this human realm came into existence. He intrinsically knows who the Guru is in this world. Only he comprehends what Gurus accomplish when they manifest in the world in this manner. It is said that to document the history of such a Guru, even if all the water in the world's oceans were churned into ink, and all the trees were uprooted to serve as pens, it would remain utterly insufficient. Thus, once the history of one individual is written, there will not be enough 'water' left here to chronicle the history of another.
Guruvani
June 1982

The history of such Gurus is what is narrated here. With what profound depth it has been articulated! How can people possibly comprehend this upon hearing it? I have already stated it—seven Gurus emerge across seven epochs. When he departs, the Divine sets him apart in such a concealed manner that no one knows what became of him, and subsequently, for the sake of future eras, he is reborn into a collective of five Gurus within a single epoch. Following that, he is brought back into the lineage of Manu and is incarnated as Manu. How can you ever conclude writing about this? That is what is referred to as the divine play or illusion of the Guru.

Obtaining the history of such Gurus did not prove beneficial to us. Consequently, we adopted the available deities like Bhadra, Kali, and Madan and worshipped them. We simply proceeded in that manner. Today, the era has changed. We must elevate ourselves in accordance with this time. We can achieve this solely through the glory of the Guru. We possess no inclination to study who such a Guru truly is. We might have studied and acquired a fair amount of knowledge. This Guru has not appeared in any of the positions delineated in that history. Then how shall we accord our respect? Such ignorance is perpetually manifesting among us. Those standing in close proximity must exercise extreme caution. Otherwise, that lifetime will be squandered for them. Why did I state that the lifetime would be squandered? Due to the ignorance of those in close proximity, harm will inevitably occur at some juncture. The mind will become suffocated. Consequently, conceptualizing something within the mind, it might occasionally translate into words and actions. With that, is not that lifetime wasted? I am stating this derived from my own experience. Thus, when such matters emerge among you, you will arrive at a scenario where you orchestrate your own destruction. You will develop arrogance akin to the arrogance that befell the children of Sri Krishna. Or you will inevitably acquire it. If you wish to prevent such an occurrence, must you not discipline yourselves through humility, love, devotion, and righteous action? Who is available for that? It is an absolute certainty that one will refuse to be humble. It is equally certain that true love, characterized as devotion, will not be mutually reciprocated. A profound obstacle will invariably be placed upon it.

Have you not observed certain ascetics (*sannyasins*) who aggressively grab hold of you upon sight? There are such individuals in the lineage of Sivananda. The moment they see you, they will embrace you. Thereafter, they will absolutely not let go. They will address you with every conceivable expression of affection and offer you everything they possibly can. One ends up consuming food beyond the capacity of one's stomach. Once they commence offering, they will not relent until it induces indigestion. They will serve food with such intense earnestness. They will meticulously perform all the requisite hospitalities. They will also exhibit the absolute embodiment of humility.

I was speaking regarding the lineage of a Guru. It is in a similar vein that I mentioned earlier that our lineage suffers from a profound impairment. What is witnessed here are the blunders that have ensued due to the administration and contemporary reforms. As a consequence of the constituent subjects growing up in a degraded state, they are devoid of refinement. Their actions are continually oscillating, merely echoing what their fathers and mothers practiced at their respective times. Because of this, it is profoundly difficult to instantly study and comprehend the Guru. However, if you are fortunate, you can comprehend and study the Guru in a single fleeting moment. If further blessed by fortune, it will eventually culminate into a profound realization.

At first sight, an inner prompting arises. An unknown love towards that person. But it will be an unfamiliar love. By unfamiliar love, it is a love we have never felt before. No one can know how it came about. After that, with further acquaintance, another feeling arises, and again, love. At the same time, what if this person does not grow? There is education, sometimes humility, sometimes love, and sometimes it seems like they have everything. But what if their mind is different? Through this acquaintance, he will be kept as an unjust person who seems old. 'Since my youth, I have drawn water for the Guru, brought him charcoal for brushing teeth, boiled water for him, and provided everything, staying with the Swami until the age of twenty-seven' - then he realized. He studied the Swami.

This is one of the deceptions of the Guru. This is said about the Guru. He stayed with that Guru until the age of twenty-seven. From a single moment - only the disciple can know what increases from that moment. However, during this time, he will clash strongly with the Guru nine times. It is like a lone elephant and a measurer assessing the magnitude of growth. Once it is seen that the step is measured, he will be pulled back by the tail. There is a problem here. The Guru will only stand according to destiny. He does whatever is appropriate for destiny at that time. Then no one has anything to do or say about it. Is it easy for a disciple to understand in this state?

A thousand disciples of a Guru will be seen in front, each asserting their own ego. One who lacks this, whether male or female, will only see one. Thus, for a perfect Guru, there will be seven people. These seven people will perceive in seven different ways. But the Guru is also a great trickster. This speaks of the Guru's deception. Having quarreled with a neighbor, one person will come to the Guru and complain that the other did this and that. The Guru will side with him, and the other will also come and complain. He will find some fault in this one too. Seeing his fault, he will scold him severely and reprimand him. What would you think if you saw this?

Even the most worthless person will come to the Guru. He might be a drunkard and a scoundrel. The Guru will stand before him as well. On the contrary, he will also stand before someone who comes to behead him like a Kapalika. There, it is the disciple who must logically protect him. At the same time, he will also stand before one who lives a moderate life. He will stand in the same way before a woman who is the greatest adulteress. If she comes groomed and adorned, like a murderous rogue elephant (as Sree Narayana Guru said), that Guru will stand before her like a mosquito. Then, how can we understand this Guru?

One person comes and says - Swami, he has encroached on my property. Another says, Swami, I trusted him, gave him everything, and loved him. Here, he has abandoned me and left. I also have three or four children. This is also said before the Guru. At the same time, a madman with a broken head has also arrived. Similarly, someone with nothing and no thoughts will come asking for today's porridge. A few perfect scholars will come together with another subject. An Ayurvedic physician, an astrologer, and a sorcerer will come as another set. Do you see the people coming to the Guru? Then there will be one who, upon seeing him from afar, falls down, prostrates at every step, and falls before him.

How long will it take to see all of them together and understand that all this is acceptable? Then it is assumed that they all have understood the Guru's deception. They will not understand. He will speak peacefully with all of them. He will stand by them as well. But if he does some little work, he will also show anger towards him. He will scold him only for what he has done. Have you seen that? It is said that one could not stand near Sree Narayana Guru Swami. It is very difficult to stand near Gurus. In this state, it is impossible to understand great souls by standing near them. Unless one stands very worthily, it is impossible to know about them.
Guruvani
July 1982

If one grows according to what is seen while going there, he will be hurt in accordance with this growth. Because faults will be found in everything he does. How to correct that? He will be corrected by getting agitated. For another person, just a look is enough. The knowledgeable one will understand from that look. The next person will be called and corrected verbally. A fourth person will be corrected by demonstrating it. For the one next to him, he will not understand through a look, nor if called and told, nor if agitated, nor if demonstrated. That is why it is said that if those standing near the Guru are not highly knowledgeable, mistakes will happen. The Guru will not give him an opportunity to repeat a mistake once pointed out. That is the Guru-disciple relationship. Then, no matter what kind, they will never do it incorrectly. Those who come like this are very few. That is why it is said 'one or two who meet the criteria'. How will people know about such a lineage of Gurus? They lack the ability to understand this. Because their past lives are not suitable for it. Understanding this, there will be two to four knowledgeable people in one place. There won't be more than that. Those four people together will control a hundred thousand people. They are placed there to control those hundred thousand people. We must obey them too. Only by obeying like that can we carry forward this tradition. Otherwise, if one asks what does it matter to him or who am I, this tradition will not continue. Sometimes what is said might be wrong. Because when interfering in many matters, mistakes will occur. Sometimes one might speak without knowing the story. Or he might be speaking when many are standing around. Then, by obeying and after being corrected two or four times, both the doer and the one causing it to be done will be corrected. Both will achieve a great state in two ways. If the opportunity to correct is never given, this will not be possible. Wherever this disobedience exists, it is finished. That lineage can do nothing. All this cannot be learned right from birth. It will only happen if we practice it and suffer inch by inch. Taking such a perfect birth, what all these great souls have suffered. We must see all that.

You have not had this kind of experience in the Guru-disciple relationship. Even if it is not your fault, you must learn all this by laying it out. A realization comes to mind that this should not be done, or said, or that it is not part of our humility, and we will move away from it. Thus, when we change ten times, there will be a turning point. When this happens a thousand times, didn't you get a hundred turning points? This is what we need in the Guru-disciple relationship. It is not that easy for us to absorb this. It can only be taken through our inclination, companionship, and that humility. This is our success. It is quite difficult to learn all this.

We have a flaw of saying, "I am standing nearby, I have seen, I have heard, I know, I have gone there," and so on. It is not something known just by seeing, hearing, or visiting. It is a culture. As long as one cannot adapt to that culture, one remains at a lower level. We usually say, "I am going to my brother-in-law's house, husband's house, or wife's house." Similarly, we say, "I am going to the bhajan mutt, to the temple, or to the ashram." I have been thinking of going to the ashram for many days, and today I have decided to go. Before going, do we think: why should I go, what should I do when I get there, how should I spend that day, how should I live for a month after returning, and what should I be until I go back? Our thoughts should be like this: I was able to go to the ashram. With what purpose should I go there? What should I achieve within a month after returning from there? How should I maintain my daily routine after coming back? What is needed when returning? If we correct ourselves every day like this, an inseparable bond with it will unknowingly be formed.

Otherwise, how would it be if it is like a dog going to the beach every day without thinking anything? There is nothing to be gained by going to a temple or an ashram like that. We must have a sense of purpose as to why we should go there. There are husbands who earn for their wives, wives who need a job, wives who do not need a job, some people who need education, wealth, and enlightenment, and those who need none of these; there are people of such various natures among both men and women. Take each of these and proceed by thinking with a sense of purpose: why am I earning, why am I working, why am I going to be a husband, why am I going to be a wife? There is no harm in that. If you do not learn all this, you will fall into a trap.

With one birth, you can eliminate multiple births or continue multiple births. That is why it is said, "Vasanamayam jagat sarvam" (The whole world is full of latent tendencies). Therefore, in order for you to contain it, sustain it, and acquire worthiness, a familiarity is being entrusted to you. That is what you need today. Learn to remove what has passed, assimilate what is present, and discard it on the point of a needle. That is possible only while alive. He will instill his resolve in it and depart. The value of life can only be understood from Gurus who teach in this manner. It cannot be learned from anyone else in the world. The more you associate with them, the more it will increase. This is success.
Guru Vani
August 1982
Birthday Message

We achieved independence through a struggle filled with sacrifice. We need to evaluate how far we have advanced through actions in the field for the fulfillment of the desire for which we gained independence. We desire to walk a little faster on the path cleared by someone else previously, whether religiously, economically, or politically. And that too, merely by looking at them, not by looking at ourselves.

In the field of education, we are following the same system created by the English and distributing some degrees. Colleges have turned into slaughterhouses. Religiously, conflicts that do not even exist there are instigated by those who live in their name or the name of that place. In that position, what was the 'Hindu' able to create for India or of India, either in the sense of India's independence for India, or in the realm of secularism as a Hindu nation with secularism as its inherent nature? Or what encouragement could be given to other religions through the Sanatana Dharma of India—through the Hindu Dharma?

We must reflect on what we are doing in accordance with the times. By 'time', I mean this era. This is the Kali Yuga. Which exponent of Dharma has stated that by proclaiming the dharma of the past three yugas, the dharma of Kali can be fulfilled? What we have been able to create in independent India are Congress from A to Z, communist movements of various colors, and political parties based on religion, caste, or narrow nationalism, such as SRP, NDP, Lok Dal, and the Muslim League.

Seeing today's political turbulence (regarding ideals and principles), one feels like saying it is akin to taking a pot of water from the sea and claiming, 'This is the ocean.' Even that remains entangled in the words of Westerners.

Is the independence we desired for all this? Was this the intention of the great souls who tried to build a secular India? Was it for this that thousands sacrificed their lives, forgetting caste and religion, without distinction of class and color? As soon as independence was achieved, didn't we have an eagerness to create religious and caste-based political parties that foster a sectarian mindset by dividing our motherland into two? Our independence is not for paving the way to the complete destruction of humanity by accumulating Western armaments. What we need is not to create class conflict by separating employers and workers into two classes. All this constitutes the face of today's India. Despite all this, we have not awakened.

It is not too late for us to awaken and act. At least now, with the enthusiasm to awaken and act, making the mind balanced so that the three instruments of mind, word, and deed can equally attain truth or prosperity, making our faith one, making our politics one, maintaining the integrity of our motherland, remembering the words of the great Thiruvalluvar who said, "One caste, one lineage, one God," or to reiterate, respecting the words of Sree Narayana Guru in Malayalam, "One caste, one religion, one God for man," determining what sacrifice we can make, religious leaders and administrative leaders joining together and standing firm in one with absolute faith, the desire for love ingrained in each of us involved in the karma of humanity or God's creation becoming one, and for the sake of that undivided 'One', thinking about how much we can act and contain ourselves by reaching the weight of the atom called 'One' in that unbroken entirety, one should take a firm resolve to work by dedicating one's lifetime for the sake of the children to come 'tomorrow'. Thus, I desire that every living being may be fortunate enough to experience the happiness of freedom and the glory brimming with the love of peace.
Guru Vani
October 1982

Our culture is at a very low level. Along with that, we were also born in an ignorant place. Knowledge has been lost in the culture of the Shudra. The time (Kali) has come for the Shudra. If this Kali is meant for the Shudra, this is a perfect opportunity to completely transform it. Through the growth of the Shudra, with the Vaishya, Kshatriya, and Brahmin mingling and living together so that everyone becomes alike, we have been given an aspect to systematically transition back to the Satya Yuga.

This is a notification given to us by God. It signifies that the growth of this Shudra is the growth of the world. When we say the growth of the world, it can only grow through a particular individual, a specific region, or a specific country. Otherwise, everyone cannot grow together simultaneously. The notification is that such an absolute individuality will certainly come to us in Kerala.

It has been explained to those in this lineage how to carry forward their faith. Merely imparting it to the ignorant will not enable them to assimilate it quickly. However, you (the knowledgeable), at least a few among you—men and women, elders and children—must come together, assimilate it, and consciously engage in the act of diligently reclaiming the prudent knowledge required to pass it on to your lineage. To facilitate this, the culture of the preceptors that has been handed down to us thus far has been presented as a medium. Subsequently, the errors that have occurred within their lineage will also be highlighted. How we can rectify these errors now—this too will be demonstrated and explained.

Today, the communities that are the most difficult to bring to the forefront are the Kuravas, Paravas, and Mukkuvas. Uplifting these groups is considered to be a formidable challenge. This knowledge has been imparted by the masters. Henceforth, you must carefully comprehend this. One must always wait for such communities with utmost vigilance. There are numerous shortcomings within these communities. Their rejection of the masters is cited as the reason for this. No matter how much we refine the Kuravas, some form of deficiency invariably manifests in them, without their own realization. When they assimilate that culture from a particular place, they tend to reject it shortly thereafter. Alternatively, they might remain aloof without absorbing it at all.

It has been impossible to uplift those engaged in occupations such as burning lime, climbing coconut trees, crafting cane products, and cobbling shoes. Regardless of the affection with which they are kept close, they eventually drift away. The Mukkuvas exhibit a similar tendency. Sage Agasthya had thoroughly understood and articulated this. Agasthya is the greatest sage the world has ever seen. He expressed it almost as a lament: "They cannot be brought forward." This clearly indicates his underlying desire to uplift them. However, it was not realized. Therefore, this effort must be integrated into our culture. They must be reformed and elevated. The divine will must also align with this endeavor. Let us pray for the same.

Beyond the three communities mentioned earlier, there may be others. Nevertheless, it is these three groups that are specifically highlighted. They can be reformed only by keeping them close. If alienated, they will never improve. Furthermore, they can only be guided forward through faith. However, even today, they retain the tendency to place their faith in and worship 'forest deities'. The situation is identical among the Mukkuvas, compounded by their ingrained tendencies. It is said that they can be reformed only if these ingrained tendencies are eradicated. It appears that many have attempted to change this. They also possess considerable knowledge. Yet, it does not become a lasting tradition for them. It is understood that the underlying cause for this is indeed a curse.

While we endeavor to establish this culture, we must not retreat upon witnessing the arrogance of the Nair. The term 'Nair' implies 'Na-Ayyar' (Not an Ayyar). Upon attaining this 'Ayyar' status, he became consumed by arrogance and deteriorated. The Ezhava also harbors a similar attitude. They are either exceedingly arrogant, or otherwise, foolish. One must not step back upon witnessing their arrogance and foolishness. As we attempt to instill this faith, we will have to endure their opposition, regardless of its magnitude. They will undoubtedly resist. Even on subjects they are ignorant about, they will speak with great eloquence. All of this is merely babble stemming from the epitome of their ignorance. Do not be swayed or intimidated by any of this. In order for them to be reformed, we must undertake any sacrifice with unwavering vigilance.

To reform the individuals belonging to the Kurava, Mukkuva, and Parava communities, we must be vigilant in ensuring that they live intermingled with others. We should create a system, even at the governmental level, to facilitate such intermingling and thereby transform their culture. There is a profound purpose behind this. Only when this occurs will the people be able to envision a unified tomorrow. Towards this end, contributions are being made to a particular cause. The headquarters of this fund is located in Dharwad. Subsequently, a new institution named the Mysore Lingayat Education Fund came into existence. Its objective, too, was the educational advancement among the Lingayats. The Mysore Lingayat Education Fund was established during a conference of Lingayats held in Bangalore in 1905 to discuss religious and secular issues.

In 1913, the Lingayats convened again in Belgaum. There were differences of opinion among the Lingayats on various matters, particularly regarding religious affairs. Consequently, the assembly decided to focus solely on educational, secular, and economic matters, and to relegate religious issues to the 'Shivayoga Mandir', which was under the control of the Jangamas.

The Lingayats did not neglect the literary branch. The commentary authored by Sripati Panditacharya on the *Vedanta Sutras*, titled *Srikara Bhashya*, serves as an example of this. From a philosophical perspective, this has been characterized as *Shakti Vishishtadvaita*. Although it is said that Renukacharya and Nilakanthacharya had written commentaries prior to this, their manuscripts have not yet been discovered.
Guruvani
November 1982

Maintaining *Brahmacharya* (celibacy/purity) is extremely difficult. The term *Brahmacharya* does not merely mean abstaining from marriage. What all is encompassed within *Brahmacharya*? If such a person commits any mistake, they will immediately feel a sense of remorse—a realization that the error occurred by their own hands. They will promptly find a resolution for it and execute it. If anyone else attempts to harm them, they will console themselves by thinking, "He is doing all this to me out of ignorance." Alternatively, even if provoked to anger in the moment, they will forgive, endure, and handle the situation gracefully. Consequently, a quality of tolerance will naturally manifest within them.

In addition to this, by being exposed to the adverse effects of such actions from numerous people, he will acquire profound experience. Through this experience, he will be able to reform a thousand people and introduce it to countless others. It is such an individual who subsequently enters *Sannyasa* (renunciation). What distance will then remain between him and a householder?

Those who are referred to as householders remain deeply estranged from true life. The majority of householders are individuals incapable of even contemplating what human life truly means. Their existence is akin to that of animals. Each of you assumes that you possess substantial knowledge, education, culture, and experience in various matters. But have you ever reflected on how true this holds when translated into your actions? Even if we leave that aside, what happens when it comes to the role of a friend? You are mutually antagonistic, devoid of humility, willing to do anything for selfish ends, and so perverse that you are incapable of living in harmony with even a single person. Then, what place is there for your knowledge, culture, or honesty? Driven by the ego of 'I', you project yourselves as symbols of a life desperately yearning to lead a mere bestial existence. Would you be pleased when this is pointed out? How can one reform an individual who leads a completely deceptive life, brimming with sheer perversity—all while constructing a facade of arrogance? You possess neither the inclination to understand this nor the capacity to assimilate it.

Like a soaring eagle, you are returning to this knowledge. At that point, the nature of the eagle will transform, and you will acquire the distinctiveness of a swan. This requires a serene intellect. No one possesses it. For instance, if you observe people seated in a gathering, you can discern where their gaze wanders. The perversions of the mind are spinning relentlessly like a machine. They are plagued by base thoughts, unable to remain steadfast or still in one place. They merely sit there; their minds are nowhere to be found in that vicinity. What can someone who spends their entire life in such a manner ever accomplish? Therefore, the knowledge to live with propriety must be cultivated first. It is that very knowledge which will nurture and elevate all of you.

The commodities in our daily use today are the culmination of the lived experiences, practices, and immense hardships of our ancestors over countless epochs. As mentioned earlier, a profound legacy of sacrifice underlies the evolution of the very garments we wear today, from their conceptual origin to their final woven form. Ponder the sheer depth of this sacrifice. Similarly, consider our customary practice of igniting a fire to cook and consume food. During an era devoid of fire, who discovered it and through what means? What constitutes its true magnificence? What immense sacrifices must have been endured to achieve this! Do we ever contemplate such matters? This applies to every single aspect of human progress. From whose intellect did all these innovations emerge? Through whose benediction were they rendered usable for us?

Take the example of clothing itself. How do we even comprehend the manner in which the conceptualization of its creation, its aesthetic appeal, and its functional utility—combined with earnest craftsmanship—came into existence? There must necessarily be a foundational concept within the mind. Who constructed that vision within the human consciousness?

Today, we possess words, alphabets, and language to effectively communicate the thoughts that arise in our minds to others. Yet, we rarely cast our gaze back to an era when communication was conducted solely by uttering a few rudimentary sounds. The emergence of alphabets, words, language, and grammar is underpinned by the sacrificial lives of numerous great visionaries. We must retrospectively examine the immense sacrifices involved in the endeavor to create these linguistic structures. Such monumental achievements were only made possible by individuals who deeply contemplated and dedicated their lives to the welfare of others.

The discovery of medicines follows an identical trajectory. It was the ascetic sages, characterized by their profound sacrifices, who discovered that a specific medicinal herb functions in a particular manner and serves the human body in a specific way. Today, armed with absolute ignorance, you have brazenly set out to mock and dismiss these very sacrificial figures. Reflect upon each of these aspects in this manner.

Despite inheriting all of this in its present advanced state, you exhibit numerous despicable behaviors driven merely by a desire to display perversity. Such behavioral aberrations must be eradicated from within you. Consequently, it is the imperative of the present age to foster a new generation that brings about a radical transformation in its knowledge, culture, and character, enabling individuals to live exemplary lives that are highly beneficial to their homes, their nation, and the world at large. Cultivating such an enlightened lineage remains the fundamental purpose and ultimate objective.
Guruvani
December 1982

Various great personages emerged and established a way of life intrinsically aligned with the environment and natural conditions of the specific regions they inhabited, structuring it in a manner profoundly beneficial to humanity. The Occidentals developed a lifestyle and culture meticulously adapted to their indigenous environment. The Orientals accomplished the exact same. The Occidentals conceptualized and structured their civilization so effectively that it would remain relevant and endure for a millennium beyond their own lifetimes. Contemplate the fact that our own lineage has evolved through a similar process. This is a legacy meant to survive for hundreds of thousands of years. Accordingly, we must forge a robust cultural heritage for our lives and our progeny. An individual living a hundred thousand years from now must still possess a memory of us and retain our cultural excellence. They must not exhibit the aforementioned perversities. If such moral degradation were to occur, all of these legacies would ultimately be rendered utterly useless to us.

For what purpose were we born here during this specific epoch? This is the critical juncture when we must deeply contemplate and act upon what we ought to contribute to our homes, our society, our nation, and the world as we mature. We must determine what benefits those who once embraced and loved us should derive from us, and similarly, what utility we should offer to those who both criticized and assisted us. Today, we may live a healthy life for perhaps ten or sixty years. Within this finite span, we encounter a multitude of life's triumphs and tribulations. We experience various degrees of social stratification and inequality. Furthermore, we often exist in complete obscurity, unknown to anyone.

Can we ever reclaim a precious moment of life that was squandered due to a perverse and degraded existence? Let each individual reflect upon the fact that it is the "I"—an ego incapable of even resolving that its mind should not inflict pain upon another or become entirely useless to them—that parades this arrogance! When we critically examine each of these aspects, we must ask: Who are we? For what purpose are we living? What is the ultimate trajectory of our existence? What intrinsic moral value do I possess to transmit to our future lineage tomorrow? Or, is there any possibility of preventing inherent flaws within myself? If such a possibility exists, from where must it be imbibed? Even if it is imbibed, what definitively ordained principles do we possess to ensure its enduring survival? Who must we aspire to become? How must that paradigm be transferred to our lineage? What relevance does this have to my own life? How far removed am I, then, from this ideal? It is imperative that each and every one of us engages in this profound introspection.

Somewhere along the line, we are hopelessly groping in profound darkness, entangled in anomalies. It is akin to a blind man aimlessly searching in the void. In such a state, the environment is hostile, and vision is entirely absent. The paramount question is how we can possibly elevate ourselves from an existence utterly devoid of alternatives. Here, the primary favorable condition is the indispensable acquisition of vision. Subsequently, the natural environment must become conducive. Just like this, despite being born as a human being into both a worthy environment and favorable circumstances, what can be done if you deliberately refuse to perceive reality? If your cognitive framework is merely oriented toward living in such a degraded state, how will you ever achieve intellectual or spiritual elevation? God has created you with every necessary qualification to assimilate all these fortuitous advantages and implement them in your life. While you ought to conduct yourself with the utmost care, ensuring that this magnificent gift of creation bestowed upon you is never tarnished, you instead eagerly hasten to engender a lineage that rapidly degenerates into a vile disposition. Who are you, unable to tolerate the sight of others living peacefully? For what purpose were you born into this world? Have you ever deeply contemplated the nature of this world or your own existence?

The sheer extent of behavioral perversity prevalent among today's school-going children becomes blatantly evident upon observing their attire and demeanor. Their parents are evidently not rearing them in accordance with our indigenous natural environment. Infants are paraded about clad in heavy gloves and socks. Our geographical environment is fundamentally distinct from that of the Occident. Our land allows for comfortable and elegant locomotion. Conversely, Occidental nations are often blanketed in thick ice and snow. They don such protective garments exclusively to withstand their harsh climatic conditions, as exposing hands and feet would precipitate frostbite. Residing in a highly favorable tropical climate, we merely observe these foreign practices and relegate ourselves to being the servile appendages of their culture. We have conspicuously failed to traverse the noble path illuminated by our ancestors through their lives of profound sacrifice, nor have we succeeded in assimilating that intrinsic goodness into our own lives. Indeed, we do not even exert the effort to do so. We are currently basking in the radiant light born of their timeless struggles and hardships. How we must internalize all of this, what substantial contributions we must make for the sake of impending generations, and what precise legacy we must forge for our lineage—these are the profound questions we must continuously ponder throughout our lives.
Guruvani
